A.
History and Development of the Company
We were incorporated in the Cayman Islands on July 19, 2019 as an exempted company with limited liability. Our principal executive offices are located at Level 15, AIA Central, No.1 Connaught Road Central, Central, Hong Kong. Our telephone number at this address is +852 2593 9309. Our registered office in the Cayman Islands is located at the offices of Portcullis (Cayman) Ltd, The Grand Pavilion Commercial Centre, Oleander Way, 802 West Bay Road, P.O. Box 32052, Grand Cayman KY1-1208, Cayman Islands. Our agent for service of process in the United States is Cogency Global Inc., located at 122 East 42nd Street, 18th Floor, New York, NY 10168.
The SEC maintains an internet site that contains reports, proxy and information statements, and other information regarding issuers that file electronically with the SEC on www.sec.gov. You can also find information on our website https://ir.bitventures.io/. The information contained on our website is not a part of this annual report.
On March 26, 2021, the Company completed its initial public offering on the Nasdaq Global Market of 3,000,000 ADSs, each representing two ordinary shares.
On June 28, 2024, the Company terminated its contractual VIE arrangements with Hywin Wealth Management, which, along with its subsidiaries, was previously the primary corporate vehicle to provide wealth management services in mainland China. The Company has completely exited from the wealth management business in mainland China.
On July 17, 2024, the Company’s name was changed from Hywin Holdings Ltd. to Santech Holdings Limited, and the trading symbol of the Company’s ADSs on Nasdaq was changed from “HYW” to “STEC.”
On August 14, 2024, the Company completely exited its businesses in overseas wealth management and asset management in Hong Kong, and disposed of certain subsidiaries in Hong Kong, namely, Haiyin Insurance (Hong Kong) Co., Limited, Hywin International Insurance Broker Limited, Haiyin International Asset Management Limited, and Hywin Asset Management (Hong Kong) Limited. After the disposals, the Company no longer holds financial service licenses in Hong Kong.
On December 5, 2024, the Company’s listing was transferred to the Nasdaq Capital Market.
On March 11, 2025, the Board of Directors resolved to remove two then-directors from the Board pursuant to the Company's Memorandum and Articles of Association and appointed two new independent directors in restructuring the Board.
On March 17, 2025, the Company issued to Carmel Holdings Limited 112,000,000 restricted ordinary shares of the Company.
On November 5, 2025, the Company announced an official launch of its e-commerce business segment.
On December 2, 2025, the Company announced that it would terminate its Deposit Agreement dated March 25, 2021 entered into between the Company and Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas as depositary for the Company’s American Depositary Shares (the “ADSs”).
On December 19, 2025, the Company held an Extraordinary General Meeting, in which shareholders approved a number of resolutions pertaining to the restructuring of the Company’s share capital and the adoption of the Company’s third amended and restated memorandum and articles of association, which included the Share Consolidation, being a share consolidation of every twenty issued and unissued ordinary shares of par value US$0.0001 each into one new consolidated ordinary share of par value US$0.0020 each, and a subsequent increase of authorized share capital to US$200,000 divided into 100,000,000 ordinary shares of par value US$0.0020 each.
On December 19, 2025, the Company’s shareholders approved the change of the Company’s name from Santech Holdings Limited to BitVentures Limited, which became effective on December 19, 2025. Effective December 24, 2025, the trading symbol of the Company’s ADSs on Nasdaq was changed from “STEC” to “BVC.”
On January 2, 2026, the Company announced that the Board had approved the official launch of the Company’s digital assets business segment. The Company began its cryptocurrency mining operations.
On January 5, 2026, the Company’s substitution listing was approved by Nasdaq. The Share Consolidation became effective, all outstanding ADSs were cancelled and exchanged for consolidated ordinary shares at the ratio of one consolidated ordinary share for every ten ADSs, and the Company’s consolidated ordinary shares of par value US$0.0020 each were listed for trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the ticker “BVC” in substitution for the ADSs.
 
Our principal capital expenditures during the three fiscal years ended June 30, 2026 consisted of purchases of digital asset mining hardware of approximately US$0.5 million in the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026. We expect to continue to acquire mining hardware in the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027, subject to market conditions and capital availability, and, as of the date of this annual report, we have no material commitments for capital expenditures.
B.
Business Overview
BitVentures Limited is a Cayman Islands holding company, with operating subsidiaries primarily in Hong Kong and the United States. We are a technology company focusing on developing early-stage technology businesses, and actively build, operate and scale our businesses in order to achieve growth. Our two principal growth segments are e-commerce and digital assets, and we seek to develop additional businesses in other areas of consumer and enterprise technology. The Company believes that early-stage technology ventures may offer exceptional growth opportunities, and seeks to identify and nurture such high-potential ventures.
During the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026, our primary businesses reported in our financial statements were e-commerce, digital assets and client referral services. In the first half of fiscal year 2026, the Company began official rollout of its e-commerce segment. The Company operated its e-commerce segment under a resale model, offering high-demand products such as consumer electronics, toys, and other consumer products via its storefront on Amazon. The Company transacted approximately US$0.14 million of gross merchandise volume (GMV) and over 1,800 customer orders in its e-commerce segment during fiscal year 2026. The Company intends to leverage its current e-commerce incubation as a launchpad for scaling additional product lines and revenue growth in its e-commerce segment. Starting in the second half of fiscal year 2026, the Company began official rollout of its digital assets segment. As of the date of this annual report, the Company has procured approximately 39 PH/s of Bitcoin (SHA-256) mining hardware and 0.3 TH/s of Scrypt-based (Litecoin and Dogecoin) mining hardware, and has currently installed an aggregate of approximately 39 PH/s of Bitcoin mining hashrate and 0.3 TH/s of Scrypt-based mining hashrate, at multiple third-party datacenter facilities in the United States with which the Company has contracted. The Company plans to continue to deploy additional mining equipment to grow its digital asset presence subject to market conditions and capital availability.
During the fiscal years ended June 30, 2024 and 2025, the Company underwent a series of restructurings to completely exit all of our legacy wealth management and asset management businesses in Hong Kong and in mainland China. On August 14, 2024, we exited our businesses in overseas wealth management and asset management and disposed of certain subsidiaries in Hong Kong, namely, Haiyin Insurance (Hong Kong) Co., Limited, Hywin International Insurance Broker Limited, Haiyin International Asset Management Limited, and Hywin Asset Management (Hong Kong) Limited. After the disposals, the Company no longer holds financial service licenses in Hong Kong. As a result of this strategic exit, for the years ended June 30, 2025 and 2024, we have reclassified our historical financial results relating to overseas wealth management and asset management services under discontinued operations. On June 28, 2024, we exited the wealth management businesses in China by terminating the variable interest entity (“VIE”) arrangements with Hywin Wealth Management, which, along with its subsidiaries, provided wealth management services in mainland China. The Company’s combined financial statements for the year ended June 30, 2024 were prepared excluding its historical PRC subsidiaries and VIEs. See “Item 4. Information on the Company—A. History and Development of the Company” for details of our corporate history.
Since fiscal year 2025, we no longer have any operations, offices or any employees in mainland China. The Company has also completely migrated its business data, information systems and business infrastructure outside of mainland China. We believe we have ceased to be a “China concept stock.”

Summary of Risk Factors
BitVentures Limited is a Cayman Islands holding company, with operating subsidiaries in Hong Kong and the United States. We are a technology company focusing on developing early-stage technology businesses, and actively build, operate and scale our businesses in order to achieve growth. The Company’s two key growth segments are currently e-commerce and digital assets, and the Company seeks to develop additional businesses in other areas of consumer and enterprise technology. The Company believes that early-stage technology ventures may offer exceptional growth opportunities, and seeks to identify and nurture such high-potential ventures.
Risks associated with our business primarily arise from our plan to develop, acquire or invest in new technology ventures. There is the risk that any technology businesses that we develop, acquire or invest in may not be successful, or such new business may not be profitable at all. In addition, any products that we develop or distribute in our e-commerce business segment might encounter a decline in value or a decrease in sales, which could adversely affect our revenues and profitability. Our operations in digital assets also subject us to heightened uncertainties and volatilities. Furthermore, our business might also be adversely affected if we are unable to comply with laws and regulations applicable to our business and services, such as laws and regulations relating to data and cybersecurity, and intellectual property. See “Item 3. Key Information—D. Risk Factors—Risks Related to Our Business.”
You should carefully consider all of the information in this annual report before making an investment in our ordinary shares. Below please find a summary of the principal risks and uncertainties we face, organized under relevant headings:
Risks Related to Our Business
●
We underwent a series of corporate restructurings in fiscal years 2024 and 2025. We are at an early stage of business transformation, and may not be able to effectively implement our future business strategies and investment, in which case our business and results of operations may be materially and adversely affected.
●
We have a history of losses and may not achieve profitability.
●
We face a number of operational and financial risks in our e-commerce business.
●
We are substantially dependent on third-party marketplaces for our e-commerce operations, and are subject to platform policies; any suspension, delisting, or policy changes could materially affect our operations.
●
We face sourcing and procurement risks in our e-commerce business.
●
We need to rely on access to third-party intellectual property, which may not be available to the Company on commercially reasonable terms, or at all.
●
As a reseller of consumer electronics, toys and other consumer products, we may be subject to product liability, warranty, and consumer product safety and advertising regulatory risk.
●
We depend on a limited number of third-party suppliers and service providers for our digital assets business, including our mining hardware manufacturer, hosting and colocation providers, power supply, and mining pool operator, and any disruption to these relationships could materially and adversely affect our business.
●
Bitcoin and other digital asset prices are highly volatile, and our reported financial results may fluctuate significantly as a result of digital asset price movements independent of our underlying operating performance.
●
We rely on a third-party custodian to safeguard the digital assets we hold, and any security breach, operational failure, or insolvency of our custodian could result in the loss of our digital assets.
●
Our future success depends on the continuing efforts to retain our existing management team and other key employees as well as to attract, integrate and retain highly skilled and qualified personnel, and our business may be disrupted if we lose their services.
●
Financial products that we historically distributed involve various risks and such risks may continue to negatively affect our reputation, client relationships, operations and prospects.
●
Our reputation and brand recognition are crucial to our business. Any harm to our reputation or failure to enhance our brand recognition may materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
●
We face risks related to outbreaks of health epidemics, natural disasters, and other extraordinary events, which could significantly disrupt our operations and adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations.
●
We and our directors and/or executive officers may be involved from time to time in legal or administrative proceedings and commercial or contractual disputes, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.
●
We have granted, and may continue to grant, share options and other forms of share-based incentive awards, which may result in increased share-based compensation expenses.
●
Any significant failure in our information technology systems could have a material adverse effect on our business and profitability.
●
Our controlling shareholder and our Chairman and Chief Executive Officer are able to exert significant influence over our Company, whose interests may differ from, or conflict with, those of our other shareholders.
●
We may face intellectual property infringement claims that could be time consuming and costly to defend and may result in the loss of significant rights by us.
●
We have limited insurance coverage.
●
If we fail to implement and maintain an effective system of internal controls to remediate our material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting, we may be unable to accurately report our results of operations, meet our reporting obligations or prevent fraud.
Risks Related to Doing Business in Hong Kong
●
Changes and developments in the political and economic policies of the PRC government may materially and adversely affect our business in Hong Kong.
●
If the PCAOB is unable to inspect or investigate completely our auditor as required under the Holding Foreign Companies Accountable Act, the SEC will prohibit the trading of our ordinary shares. The delisting of our ordinary shares, or the threat of their being delisted, may materially and adversely affect the value of your investment. Additionally, the inability of the PCAOB to conduct adequate inspections of our auditor would deprive our investors of the benefits of such inspections.
●
The PRC government may intervene or influence the Hong Kong operations of an offshore holding company, such as ours, at any time. The PRC government may exert more control over offerings conducted overseas and/or foreign investment in Hong Kong-based issuers.
